newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Saudi oil minister says OPEC committed to quota pact.
newsitem.headline: Saudi oil minister says OPEC committed to quota pact.

text.p: Saudi Arabian Oil Minister Ali Naimi said on Wednesday that the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) had secured a complete commitment to honour quotas from the 11 members.
He was among OPEC leaders to comment to reporters on Wednesday's decision to freeze current quotas under a ceiling of 25.03 million barrels daily for six more months from July 1.
Western industry monitors report that actual volume has recently been some two million above this, with Venezuela and Nigeria among the biggest over-producers.
""We have a very high level of commitment...one hundred percent," Naimi said.
The Libyan president of OPEC, Abdullah Salem al-Badri, said that production "should go down" as a result of promises given in Vienna.

Al-Badri said that ministers had "one by one" given assurances that they would adhere to quotas. "It was a very frank meeting," he said. "We can have a stick for the ministers or we believe them - and I believe them".
Oil Minister Amir Rasheed of Iraq was also questioned about the lack of any OPEC mechanism to coerce sovereign states into abiding by their agreements.
"We got their assurances and that is more efficient than any mechanism," he said.
